To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression patterns of genes in liver tumors of AOX-/- (spontaneous) and ciprofibrat (induced) mice are similar to each other but different from DENA-induced liver tumors.

the expression profiles of liver tumors induced by the non-genotoxic perioxisome proliferator ciprofibrate are similar to the expression profiles of tumors that develop spontaneously in peroxiome deficient mice, and that the expression profiles in liver tumors from peroxisome deficient mice are distinct from the expression profiles of genotoxic carcinogen-induced tumors.

we have identified 12 genes up-regulated in all three classes (AOX- and ciprofibrated-induced, and DENA-induced) of liver tumors and that we have identified distinguishing features between non genotoxic and genotoxic liver carcinogen derived liver tumor as well as genes up-regulated both in both types of tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying molecular markers for the diagnosis and early detection of liver tumors, as well as for understanding the molecular mechanisms involved in the pathogenesis of liver tumors.
the identification and analysis of genes involved in hepatocarcinogenesis and the development of molecular markers for early diagnosis and prognosis of HCC.
the molecular basis for hepatocarcinogenesis in the AOX-(-) mouse model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the gene expression profiles of liver tumors in mice are not only dependent on the type of carcinogen but also on the type of tumor, and that the expression profile of a given tumor may be a function of the tumor stage.

the gene expression profile of liver tumors developing spontaneously in the absence of AOX in the AOX-(-/-) mouse is similar to the gene expression profile in liver tumors induced by ciprofibrate, a non-genotoxin peroxisome profilerator, but not by DENA, a genotoxin.
the expression profiles of AOX-/- HCCs are more similar to those induced by cirofibrate than to those induced by DENA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the expression of PPARalpha regulated genes in liver, and in particular those participating in lipid metabolism, appears to be a critical factor in the development of hepatocellular carcinoma in AOX- and ciprofibrated mice.

the expression profiles of HCCs developing spontaneously in AOX- mice share a number features with ciprofibrat-induced liver tumors but differ from DENA-induced liver tumors, and that the activation of peroxysome proliferator- activated receptor alpha and PPARalpha regulated genes are key factors in the genesis of these tumors.
the expression profile of HCCs developing spontaneously in AOX- mice is similar to that induced by a non-genotoxic carcinogen ciprofibrate and different from that induced by a genotoxin, DENA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed an animal model of liver tumorigenesis that is based on a spontaneous process and that is not dependent upon the administration of exogenous agents.
we have identified a number of genes that are up or down regulated in the AOX- mouse model of liver cancer.
the activation of the PPARalpha pathway is a key feature in the development of liver tumors induced either by a peroxi-some proliferator or by a spontaneous loss of AOX function.
